title: OKF Civic Profile (civic/0.6) record schema
description: Validates a record's frontmatter against core OKF v0.2 plus the x-civic civic/0.6 profile. Core OKF requires only `type`; the profile requires four fields, and only on a record whose type is `org`. Everything else is optional and additive. Nothing here may cause a consumer to reject a document: OKF v0.2 §11 requires tolerance of unknown keys, so this schema deliberately does NOT set additionalProperties:false at the document level.

synthetic.description: Producer key, not part of x-civic. True when the record describes a fabricated thing. Marked at record level because files get separated from their collection README. Proposed for core OKF rather than the profile: 'is this real' is not civic-specific.

stale_after.description: OKF v0.2 §5.5. Absolute date; the record is stale when today >= this.

verified.description: OKF v0.2 §5.2. A list of verification events, or a single bare mapping which consumers MUST treat as a one-element list. Its ABSENCE is meaningful: no `verified` key is the `unverified` trust tier (§5.3) and MUST NOT cause rejection.

sources.description: OKF v0.2 §5.1. Per-claim attribution is by markdown footnote keyed to `sources[].id`.

allOf.comment: A record carrying an x-civic block must declare which profile version it conforms to.
THE profile requirement: an organization record carries exactly these four fields plus the declaration. Nothing else in this schema is required.
`timestamp` was superseded by `generated.at` in OKF v0.2 (§13.1).

actor.description: OKF v0.2 §7. `<producer>/<version>` for agents and tools, `human:<id>` for a person, `process:<id>` for an automated process. Trust tiers key off the `human:` prefix.

id.description: Stable key used to attribute individual claims from the body via a `[^id]` footnote. Keyed rather than positional so reordering the list cannot silently misattribute.

resource.description: A followable artifact (URL or bundle-relative path) OR a scope descriptor it cannot follow.

xcivic.description: The civic profile namespace. A generic OKF consumer ignores this entire object; per §11 its contents can never make a bundle non-conformant with core OKF.

subject.description: REQUIRED on an org record. Candid PCS Subject facet — what the organization does. Codes must exist in the taxonomy; scripts/validate.py resolves them against the vendored subset.

population.description: REQUIRED on an org record. Candid PCS Population facet — who the organization serves.

org_type.description: REQUIRED on an org record. Candid PCS OrgType facet. Use a level-1 parent deliberately where no child matches the legal form, and say so in org_type_note.

registration_country.description: REQUIRED on an org record. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Distinct from operating geography.

provides.description: Optional. The specific function the organization offers — the substitution and matching axis. No controlled vocabulary yet; see the profile's open questions.

registration.description: Optional. Deliberately not required: an organization with no usable registry record must remain representable.

budget_currency.description: Optional, ISO 4217. An amount without a currency is not a fact. Amounts are never pre-converted.

situation.description: Optional. Slug of a shared place node. Community context belongs to the place, not to each organization operating there.

ntee.description: Optional enrichment. A US IRS vocabulary: it cannot reach non-US organizations, so a rollup on it silently under-covers a mixed corpus.

relations.description: Optional. ASSERTED organization-to-organization edges only — relationships that cannot be computed. Substitution and complementarity are derived from provides + situation + population and are deliberately not stored.

verifiable_by.description: Optional. Who could answer 'how do I know this?'. Distinct from `sources`, which says where a claim came from. A bundle carries a path toward validation, not a passport.
